manifest.name: dsh-browser
manifest.description: Tabbed browser panel for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI: DeepSeek search, workspace-bound browsing profiles, declarative extensions, a sandboxed page renderer and downloads.
manifest.author: Plonkloving

readme.text:
A browser panel for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) Web UI. It is a Cordis bundle: a Host half that adds fenced HTTP routes and one agent tool, and a web Client half that registers a `browser` main panel plus a rail icon.

中文说明见 [README.zh.md](README.zh.md).

```sh
dsh plugin add Plonkloving/dsh-browser
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle` (`cordis.patch.yml` inserts one Host row) and `dsh.client` (the web half). There is no build step and no runtime dependency: the Client bundle is plain JavaScript loaded through `window.__ModuleLoader__`.

After installing, the rail icon (a globe, after *Plugins* and *Schedules*) opens the panel.
**Host-side edits need a row reload** — disable and re-enable the plugin row, or restart the Harness: the Loader keeps the imported ES module. Client edits reload through HMR.

- Back / forward / reload / home, a tab strip, and an omnibox that treats input as a URL, a workspace file path, or a search query.
- `Ctrl`/`⌘`-click, middle-click and `Alt`+`Enter` open a new tab (Shift keeps it in the foreground). The same intent is reported from inside rendered pages.
- Browser state — profiles, tabs, bookmarks, history, extension switches, download records — is stored in this origin's `localStorage` under `dsh-browser.state.v1`.

The omnibox calls `POST /dshbrowse/api/search`, which runs `ctx.web.search` through the Harness web seam (the configured provider, `deepseek-official`, uses the native `web_search` server tool). The panel renders the returned `sources[]` natively and can export the list as CSV or JSON. Results are cached per query for the session, so the same search does not cost a second model call.

| View | How |
| --- | --- |
| **Page** (default) | `GET /dshbrowse/api/render?url=…` fetches the page with `ctx.web.fetch`, injects a `<base>` pointing at the real site so its CSS, images and fonts resolve, strips the site's scripts and its `meta` CSP / refresh, appends a navigation bridge, and returns the document from the panel's own origin. The frame is `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-downloads allow-modals"` — no `allow-same-origin`, so the document keeps an opaque origin. |
| **Reader** | `GET /dshbrowse/api/page` returns the same fetch verbatim; the client parses it with `DOMParser` into a document model (h1–h6, p, li, pre, img, table, links) that extensions can rewrite. |

Because the framed document is served from the panel origin, a site's `X-Frame-Options` / `frame-ancestors` no longer applies. The trade-off is that site JavaScript is stripped: a client-rendered SPA may need Reader instead.

- `GET /dshbrowse/api/files?dir=…` lists one directory; `GET /dshbrowse/api/file?path=…` serves one file. HTML/CSS are rewritten so a generated report keeps its stylesheet, images and scripts; everything else is streamed with the right content type and `no-cache`.
- Root paths only: a canonical path outside every registered workspace directory (and the downloads folder) is refused with 403.
- HTML, SVG/PNG/JPEG/WebP, PDF, Markdown, plain text, JSON/CSV, video and audio are rendered inline; the new-tab page and a dedicated file browser list them.
- `POST /dshbrowse/api/inbox` consumers: the `browser_open` tool queues a URL or a workspace file and the panel opens it in a tab.

A Chrome-style, declarative extension system:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `permissions` | shown in the manager, informational |
| `contentScripts[].matches` | `*`, `*://host/*` patterns decide where a script applies |
| `contentScripts[].hide` | CSS selectors removed before the document model is built |
| `contentScripts[].highlight(s)` | words marked in the reader |
| `contentScripts[].width` | reader width |
| `action` | gives the extension a toolbar button and a panel |

Extensions cannot execute code. Built in: ad/tracker cleanup, keyword highlighting, focus reading (paragraph limit), page outline. The manager installs from a pasted `manifest.json`, enables/disables, removes, and offers three suggested manifests.

| Entry point | Product |
| --- | --- |
| Page → download | page HTML (relative references rewritten to absolute URLs), article Markdown, article plain text |
| File page → download | the workspace file; a copied HTML page has its relative references rewritten to `file:///` paths so it still renders |
| Search results | CSV or JSON of the source list |
| Settings | one JSON with profiles, bookmarks, history, extensions and settings |
The target is `$DSH_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD_DIR`, else the system Downloads folder (`Downloads`, `下载`, `downloads`). That folder is also a browse root, so a saved file can be reopened in a tab.

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /search` | `ctx.web.search` |
| `GET /page` | `ctx.web.fetch`, raw body |
| `GET /render` | fetched page as a framed, script-free document |
| `GET /files` | list a directory inside an allowed root |
| `GET /file` | serve/stream one allowed file |
| `POST /download` | write `{kind: file \| url \| text}` to the Downloads folder |
| `GET /inbox` | queued `browser_open` requests |

All of them hang off `/dshbrowse/api` and run behind the Harness browser-trust fence (`ctx.connection.requestRejection`), the same check the built-in `/api` channel uses. Nothing is proxied through a third party.

- Every route is refused unless the request passes `ctx.connection.requestRejection`.
- Path admission: `realpath` the request, then require containment in a registered workspace directory or the downloads folder; traversal and symlink escapes answer 403.
- Rendered and local pages run in a sandboxed frame without `allow-same-origin`, so their markup cannot reach the Harness API even though it is served from the panel origin. Proxied pages additionally have their scripts stripped.
- Extension manifests only contribute selectors, words and a width; there is no code execution path.
- Download file names are sanitized and writes never overwrite.

```
dsh-browser/
├── package.json        dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client
├── cordis.patch.yml    inserts one Host row (id: dsh-browser)
├── index.js            Host: routes + browser_open tool

- Host services: `web`, `webServer`, `connection` (required), `tools` (optional — enables `browser_open`).
- Client injections: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout` (declares `main` and `sidebar.panellist`), `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale`.
- No `dependencies`; the official `@deepseek-ai/*` packages resolve from the installation.
